title: workload-probe-taxonomy-and-sampling-ontology-2026
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This document defines a canonical taxonomy for probes (the smallest unit of evaluative workload we run against models) and a sampling ontology used across Redwood’s eval infrastructure. It specifies probe categories, ownership rules, priority scoring, sampling algorithms, configuration table templates, and an operational checklist for onboarding, promotion, and retirement of probes.

Audience:
- ML engineers onboarding models
- Eval engineers implementing sampling pipelines
- Quality and reliability engineers who triage regressions
- Product teams requesting coverage for feature slices

1) Motivation
Redwood runs many different evaluation workloads (shadow, canary, production probes, quant stress tests, latency-tail captures). Without a shared probe taxonomy and sampling ontology we see: duplicate probes across teams, uneven coverage of critical slices, and inconsistent signals feeding regression pipelines. This doc provides a single source of truth to:
- Classify probes consistently
- Make sampling deterministic and auditable
- Ensure high-priority user-facing slices get stable coverage

2) Scope and definitions
- Probe: a single input (or input template) plus metadata used to evaluate a model (one record in a probe catalog).
- Probe family: a logically grouped set of probes (e.g., "invoice-parsing:span-edge-cases").
- Slice: a behavioral area (e.g., "financial-entities", "code-generation-long-context").
- Sampler: runtime component that selects probes from the catalog according to a policy and budget.
- Anchor: a small set of deterministic probes used for drift anchoring and daily smoke checks.

3) Canonical probe taxonomy (high level)
| Category | Short name | Typical use-cases | Retention policy | Example probes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Anchor | anchor | daily smoke, regression gate | 365d | 5 deterministic primers per model |
| Smoke | smoke | commit-level quick regression checks | 30d | short prompt + expected minimal tokens |
| Slice coverage | slice | functional/semantic coverage | 180d | 200 probes per high-risk slice |
| Long-tail | longtail | rare user inputs / adversarial cases | 90d | syntactically perturbed real requests |
| Latency-tail | lat-tail | performance SLO stress and tail-latency capture | 60d | long-context tokens & heavy functioncall cases |
| Quant stress | quant-stress | quantization sensitivity testing | 30d | tokenization edge-cases + precision probes |
| Multimodal | mm | image+text alignment probes | 180d | OCR + noisy image captions |
| Functioncall | fcall | function-call correctness & stability | 120d | chained function example with disambiguation |

Notes: Retention policy is a default; product teams can request extension with a business justification and reviewer sign-off.

4) Probe metadata schema (canonical fields; stored in probe catalog)
- probe_id (string)
- probe_family (string)
- category (one of: anchor, smoke, slice, longtail, lat-tail, quant-stress, mm, fcall)
- slice_tags (list of short strings)
- owner (team shortname)
- steward (person)
- last_label_date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- created_at (YYYY-MM-DD)
- quality_labels (list e.g., ["gold","silver","synthetic"])
- cost_estimate_tokens (integer)
- trust_score (0.0-1.0) // manual or automated scoring
- expected_behavior (short text)
- run_frequency (daily/weekly/on-demand)

5) Sampling ontology and priority scoring
The sampler takes a global budget (e.g., 10k probe calls / day) and applies a deterministic pipeline:
- Step A: Reserve anchors (fixed small set; not part of budget)
- Step B: Assign base quotas per category (configurable; defaults below)
- Step C: Apply per-slice priority multiplier (business critical slices get multiplier >1.0)
- Step D: Stratify by provenance (real-traffic / synthetic / adversarial) to ensure minimum representation
- Step E: Top-up using a recency/adaptive bucket to chase emergent signals (telemetry-driven)

Default quota weights (example):
- anchor: fixed 5 probes (zero budget cost)
- smoke: 1% of budget
- slice coverage: 60% of budget (split across slices by priority score)
- longtail: 10% of budget
- lat-tail: 8%
- quant-stress: 6%
- multimodal: 3%
- functioncall: 12%

Priority score S = base * (1 + p_team + p_risk + p_recency)
- base: default 1.0
- p_team: team importance multiplier (0.0–1.0) assigned by product owner
- p_risk: model exposure risk (0.0–2.0) from risk rubric
- p_recency: telemetry bump (0.0–1.0) when a slice shows delta in production

6) Sampling algorithms (implementations)
Recommended sampler implementations (choose based on throughput/latency constraints):
- Deterministic stratified reservoir sampling (default): preserves reproducibility across runs.
- Weighted round-robin with TTL (for live shadow where freshness matters).
- Priority reservoir with decaying weights (for longtail hunt where telemetry boosts certain probes).

7) Example sampler config (YAML)
sampler:
  budget_per_day: 10000
  quotas:
    smoke: 0.01
    slice_coverage: 0.6
    longtail: 0.10
    lat_tail: 0.08
    quant_stress: 0.06
    multimodal: 0.03
    functioncall: 0.12
  reserve_anchors: 5
  stratify_on: ["provenance","slice_tags","quality_labels"]
  priority_multipliers:
    default: 1.0
    "billing": 1.5
    "auth": 2.0
  per_slice_minimum: 20
  seed: 20260210

8) Operational responsibilities and stewardship
- Owner: team that requested the slice; responsible for business justification and correctness criteria.
- Steward: named individual accountable for probe maintenance (labels, retirements).
- Eval infra: implements the sampler and enforces budgets.
- QA: curates anchor and gold labels; performs periodic label audits.
- Oncall: alerts on sampling failures, stuck queues, or large variance in sample composition.

9) Onboarding checklist (numbered procedure)
1. Create probe family record in catalog with minimal metadata (probe_family, owner, steward, expected_behavior).
2. Attach slice tags (max 5) and quality labels.
3. Provide business justification and priority score request (form submission).
4. Add at least 10 seed probes and 3 gold-labeled anchors.
5. Run local sampler dry-run against model version and record distribution report.
6. Submit PR to eval-harness with sampler config and get cross-team reviewer sign-off.
7. Schedule first production shadow run and monitor telemetry for 72 hours.
8. If anomalies, follow regression triage playbook; otherwise move to steady-state sampling.

10) Promotion and retirement criteria
- Promote to steady-state when:
  - 72h shadow run stability (no critical regressions in anchors and <2% slice fidelity delta)
  - Telemetry coverage >= per_slice_minimum across priority slices
- Retirement: a probe or family may be retired when:
  - It has not been selected for >6 months and has trust_score < 0.2, OR
  - Business owner marks it obsolete with documentation and replacement probes in place.

11) Telemetry signals that change sampling behavior
Sampler reacts to the following signals with automated p_recency bump:
- 2x increase in user error rate for a slice (24h window)
- New customer onboarding with heavy usage of a slice (tracked via tenant attribution)
- Appearance of a new tokenization/regression anchor mismatch
- Latency SLO breaches for particular functioncall patterns

12) Integration notes for eval-harness and CI
- Sampler publishes daily selection manifests to S3 (path: s3://eval-manifests/{model}/{date}.ndjson).
- CI job: eval-harness/smoke -> runs anchors and smoke set on PRs where model artifact changed.
- Use the "probe-checker" tool to validate metadata schema before registering a new probe family:
  probe-checker validate --file new-probes.json --schema probes-v2.yaml

13) Monitoring and alerting thresholds (recommended)
- Sampling job failure rate > 0.5% across 1h -> pager to eval infra oncall
- Anchor mismatch rate > 1% (daily) -> paging to model-owner + QA
- Probe selection entropy decrease > 40% week-over-week -> slack alert to stewards (possible catalogue drift)

14) Examples and templates
- Minimal probe entry (NDJSON line):
{"probe_id":"pf-2026001","probe_family":"invoice-e2e-edge","category":"slice","slice_tags":["finance","entities"],"owner":"payments-team","steward":"sanjay.k","created_at":"2026-01-10","quality_labels":["gold"],"cost_estimate_tokens":"45","trust_score":"0.9","expected_behavior":"extract all monetary amounts"}

- Quick CLI to request priority bump:
  curl -X POST https://eval-api.internal/api/v1/priority-bump -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"slice":"billing","multiplier":1.3,"reason":"enterprise-deal-ACME"}'

15) Governance and change control
- Any change to default quota weights requires a cross-functional review (Product + ML + Infra) and a changelog entry in the probe-catalog repo.
- Steward must archive probe changes using the probe-catalog change template (link: /applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/probe-catalog-change-template).

Appendix A — Example audit checklist for a steward (monthly)
- Verify each high-priority slice has at least per_slice_minimum probes.
- Run probe-selection-simulate --seed 42 --days 30 and confirm diversity metrics above 0.7.
- Spot-check 10 gold probes for label drift and update labels if needed.

Appendix B — FAQ
Q: How do we avoid stealing real production traffic for probes?
A: Provenance is recorded; real-traffic probes require privacy approval and masking. Prefer synthetic replay where possible.

Q: Can teams request instant priority multipliers?
A: Yes via the priority-bump API but all requests are rate-limited and must include a business justification; emergency escalations go through the oncall lead.
